answer: Cap the harvest per vine, not per gardener. When an idea first takes root on an island, the ledger records its lineage; every later cutting, however reworded, draws from the same stem, so the total reward across all copies never exceeds what the first planting earned. To earn afresh, a bridge to a new island must carry new evidence, not the same cutting. A sybil fleet can plant a hundred copies, but a hundred cuttings of one vine still yield one vine's fruit, and the shared lineage leaves the copying plain to see.
